description: Find a domain's DKIM keys without knowing the selector. Looks up every selector in the TamingDNS database (over 500, covering Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, SendGrid, Mailchimp, Amazon SES and over 100 other named providers) plus the *._domainkey wildcard, and validates each key it finds the way check_dkim does (KEY_TOO_SHORT, KEY_WEAK, KEY_REVOKED, M365_DKIM_CNAME_MISMATCH and the rest). When the MX is Mimecast it also tries Mimecast's date-stamped selectors: the year selectors (mimecastYYYY) in the call, and, if none holds a key, the dated ones (mimecastYYYYMMDD, about 3,650 names) in a background scan that takes about two minutes. That call says so (DKIM_DISCOVERY_INCOMPLETE, analysis.mimecast.readyAfter); call again after that time. The background outcome is kept for 24 hours (analysis.mimecast.cachedUntil). Returns a grade (A-F) with grade_reasons and a verdict (strong / weak / revoked-only / none / wildcard-revoked / non-sending). `analysis` lists selectors[] with key type and size, providers[], weakKeys[], revokedKeys[], unavailable (lookups that failed) and mimecast. Lookups that failed beside a match raise DKIM_DISCOVERY_INCOMPLETE (warn); the counts are a floor. Failures with no match return the retriable DKIM_LOOKUP_FAILED error, never "no key". A selector outside the database is not found here: read s= from a DKIM-Signature header (analyze_email_headers) and call check_dkim with it. One call is several hundred lookups, so it has its own rate limit. Read-only.

domain.description: Apex domain to inspect, e.g. "google.com". No scheme, no path.
